title: Completed proper base change is Frobenius-equivariant
statement:
For every Frobenius-equivariant square and Weil tower datum,

$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}\Theta_S
=\Theta_T\Phi_{Y'}
(\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}):
\Phi_{Y'}S\longrightarrow T.
$$

If all four Frobenius automorphisms and all pullback/exchange comparisons are
identities, then $\vartheta_n$ is an ordinary compatible endomorphism and
this equation specializes exactly to the operator naturality of the finite
rectangle and its product-cone limit. For nonidentity Frobenius, no
identification of $\Phi_XK_n\to K_n$ with an endomorphism $K_n\to K_n$ is
made.

proof.text: Write $\Phi=\Phi_{Y'}$. The formulas in [def-weil-pbc-completed-frobenius-structures] give, with right-to-left composition, $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}\Theta_S=(tWs)(s^{-1}\Theta_{A,\infty}\Phi(s))=tW\Theta_{A,\infty}\Phi(s)$, since $ss^{-1}=1$. For the other composite, $\Theta_T\Phi(\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}})=t\Theta_{D,\infty}\Phi(t^{-1})\Phi(t)\Phi(W)\Phi(s)=t\Theta_{D,\infty}\Phi(W)\Phi(s)$, since a functor preserves composition and identities and $t^{-1}t=1$. Both composites have source $\Phi S$ and target $T$.

The product-cone statement [lemma-weil-pbc-frobenius-product-cone-limit] gives $W\Theta_{A,\infty}=\Theta_{D,\infty}\Phi_{Y′}(W)$. Precompose this equality with $\Phi_{Y′}(s)$ and postcompose with $t$. This gives precisely the equality of the two composites in step 1.

source.place: ## Proof, sentence “They are equal by the product-cone Frobenius equation.”

proof.text: Under the identity assumptions, the compatibility equation in [def-weil-pbc-frobenius-tower-datum] becomes $r_{n+1,n}\vartheta_{n+1}=\vartheta_nr_{n+1,n}$, so $\vartheta_\bullet$ is an ordinary compatible tower endomorphism. The formulas in [def-weil-pbc-frobenius-corner-structures] become $\vartheta_{E,n}=L(g')^*\vartheta_n$, $\Theta_{B,n}=Lg^*Rf_*\vartheta_n$, $\Theta_{D,n}=Rf'_*L(g')^*\vartheta_n$, $\Theta_{A,n}=h_n^{-1}\Theta_{B,n}h_n$, and $\Theta_{C,n}=(h'_n)^{-1}\Theta_{D,n}h'_n$. The equations of [lemma-weil-pbc-frobenius-level-rectangle] now read $h_n\Theta_{A,n}=\Theta_{B,n}h_n$, $v_n\Theta_{A,n}=\Theta_{C,n}v_n$, $h'_n\Theta_{C,n}=\Theta_{D,n}h'_n$, and $v'_n\Theta_{B,n}=\Theta_{D,n}v'_n$. Its composite assertion reads $(v'_nh_n)\Theta_{A,n}=\Theta_{D,n}(v'_nh_n)$, with the identical common map after replacing $v'_nh_n$ by $h'_nv_n$. These are the ordinary intertwining equations of [lemma-weil-pbc-level-map-operator-naturality]; that statement is used to identify their form, not to infer a global endomorphism of $K$ from the family $\vartheta_n$. The displayed limit formula in [lemma-weil-pbc-frobenius-product-cone-limit] becomes $\Theta_{Z,\infty}=R\varprojlim_n\Theta_{Z,n}$, since the canonical comparison for the identity functor is identity; its equation becomes $W\Theta_{A,\infty}=\Theta_{D,\infty}W$. Conjugating by $s,t$ as in step 1 gives exactly ordinary operator naturality on the completed source and target. This identifies the finite and limit equations directly; it does not assume that an arbitrary family $\vartheta_n$ is already the reduction of a chosen endomorphism of $K$. Without the identity assumptions, all maps retain source $\Phi_Z$ of the relevant object, and none of these specializations is made.
